newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt plans to form holding structure - paper.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt plans to form holding structure - paper.

text.p: German retail group Karstadt AG plans to move to a holding structure as soon as it completes its integration of the Hertie department store chain, the newspaper Welt am Sonntag reported on Sunday.

Preparations were already under way to integrate the Hertie stores more directly with Karstadt's four divisions, the newspaper said, citing management board chairman Walter Deuss and supervisory board chief Guido Sandler.
A supervisory board meeting at Hertie last week had decided to cut the unit's 200-strong central administrative team down to 50, it said.
Welt am Sonntag said the Hertie stores would, however, remain part of Hertie Waren und Kaufhaus GmbH group for the time being and the Hertie name would be retained.
The organisational changes would be discussed at a meeting of Karstadt's supervisory board on November 7 as well as a reshuffle of responsibilities on the management board.

Karstadt has been burdened by the costs of integrating Hertie since it acquired the rival chain in January 1994, although it managed to raise its net profit to 109.2 million marks in 1995 from a depressed 41.9 million in 1994.
